content.title: Who was the Fab Five? Revisiting Michigan’s iconic 1993 squad that featured Jalen Rose, Chris Webber | Sporting News Canada
content.text: JUMP TO: Who was the Fab Five?How many of the Fab Five played in the NBA?Did the Fab Five ever win a championship?Fab Five controversiesAcross college basketball history, there are plenty of starting fives that have reached an all-time status through their dominance. Perhaps no starting lineup, though, has ever been as iconic as the Fab Five. Michigan's 1991 recruiting class is praised as one of the greatest of all time, led by a group of five players that didn't just have the rare opportunity to all start as freshmen, but took advantage of it by leading the Wolverines to multiple dominant seasons.With its talented starting unit that was eventually dubbed the Fab Five, Michigan was a focal point of the college basketball world in the early 1990s.Here's everything to know about the Fab Five, from the members of the lineup to the controversies that surrounded Michigan with the unit.MORE: Which schools have the most March Madness wins?Who was the Fab Five?The Fab Five was a group of five players in Michigan's 1991 recruiting class that quickly went on to start together, becoming an elite college basketball squad. The five members are as follows:F Chris WebberF Juwan HowardG/F Ray JacksonG Jalen RoseG Jimmy KingThose five players started together for Michigan for the 1991-92 and 1992-93 seasons. Webber was the first to leave; the other four remained with the Wolverines in 1993-94, while just Jackson and King stayed for 1994-95.The Fab Five became the first team in NCAA history to compete in a national championship with a unit of all-freshman starters. Along the way, they drew plenty of attention, both for their success as a team but also for their antics on and off the court. The unit had an ESPN documentary made about it in 2011 named "The Fab Five."As freshmen in 1991-92, Michigan's young stars actually didn't become the full-time starting unit until February. But once the first-year players clicked, they remained the starters. That season, Rose led the way with 17.6 points per game, while Webber (15.5 points per game) and Howard (11.1 points per game) followed. The Wolverines went 25-9 and reached the NCAA Tournament's title game with the Fab Five as freshmen. In 1992-93, Michigan went 31-9 and again reached March Madness' championship. But both of those accomplishments, along with some more wins, were later vacated by the NCAA due to a recruiting scandal.After Webber left the Fab Five for the NBA following the 1992-93 season, the remaining four starters led Michigan to a 24-8 record and Elite Eight appearance in 1993-94. With just Jackson and King remaining in 1994-95 though, the Wolverines went 17-14 and lost in the first round of the NCAA Tournament.At one point, the group of Webber, Rose, Howard, King and Jackson wanted to be known as "Five Times." Instead, they earned one of the most iconic nicknames for a lineup in sports history, the Fab Five, which reached its peak in 1993 with its second consecutive title game appearance.MORE: How 'One Shining Moment' became a March Madness anthemHow many of the Fab Five played in the NBA?Four of the five players in the Fab Five would later play in the NBA. Ray Jackson did not reach the league; he was cut by the Knicks prior to the 1995-96 season and later cut by the Pistons. He also played in the Continental Basketball Association for some time.Nowadays, Jackson lives in Austin, Texas, and runs a moving company and a nonprofit organization that helps children on and off the basketball court.Here's a brief look at how the other four Fab Five players fared in the NBA:Chris WebberWebber was selected first overall in the 1993 NBA Draft, traded on draft night to the Warriors. He would spent the majority of his career with the Kings, averaging over 20 points per game for his 15-year career.Webber was a five-time All-Star in the NBA and was named a Hall of Famer in 2021. He's now an analyst for TNT.Jalen RoseRose was selected 13th overall by the Nuggets in the 1994 NBA Draft. However, he spent most of his NBA years with the Pacers; he reached three consecutive Eastern Conference Finals with Indiana in the late 1990s, also playing in the 2000 NBA Finals.Since 2007, Rose has been a basketball analyst. He was with ABC and ESPN until 2023.Juwan HowardHoward was selected fifth overall in the 1994 NBA Draft by the Bullets. He played for eight different teams in 16 seasons, averaging just over 13 points per game.In 2012, Howard won an NBA title on the LeBron James-led Heat, becoming the only Fab Five member to win a championship. He would spend a few seasons with Miami as an assistant coach as well.In 2019, Howard became the head coach at Michigan. The Wolverines made two NCAA Tournaments in his tenure, but he was fired in 2024 after an 8-24 season.Jimmy KingKing was selected 35th overall in the 1995 NBA Draft by the Raptors. He appeared in 64 games for Toronto and Denver, but retired after the 1996-97 season. In 2006, King said he was working on Wall Street as a financial analyst, and he's also been a radio color commentator covering Michigan in the past.MORE: Who are college basketball's highest-paid coaches?Did the Fab Five ever win a championship?Despite reaching two national championship games, the Fab Five never won a title. Michigan won the 1989 championship, which was just a few years before the Fab Five arrived on campus.As freshmen and sophomores, the Fab Five helped the Wolverines make deep March runs. In 1992, they lost 71-51 to Duke in the national championship. The following year, they lost 77-71 to North Carolina in the title game.Once Webber left after the 1992-93 season, Michigan didn't make it past the Elite Eight, falling in that round to Arkansas in 1994.MORE: Most March Madness wins ever, by coachFab Five controversiesThe Fab Five were known for their trash talk, with their ESPN documentary offering some insight into how they criticized Duke players around the time of the 1992 national championship matchup.The controversy surrounding the Fab Five extends beyond the court. Michigan was the subject of a significant NCAA investigation in the late 1990s that was focused on players directly receiving thousands of dollars from Ed Martin, a booster for the school.By 1999, four players were called before a federal grand jury to answer questions about the investigation. It was discovered that Michigan players Maurice Taylor, Robert Traylor, Louis Bullock and Webber borrowed a total of $616,000 from Martin, compromising their amateur status. Rose was also called in front of the grand jury, but didn't accept more than a few thousand dollars total from Martin.Michigan had severe repercussions from the scandal. Head coach Steve Fisher was fired in 1997, and the Wolverines placed their basketball program on two years probation, withdrawing from 2002-03 postseason consideration. It also vacated the accomplishments of most of the previous five seasons and removed players' names from its record books.The NCAA also punished Michigan by penalizing it one scholarship spot for four seasons and ordering it to disassociate from the players related to the scandal. In total, Michigan's 1988 Big Ten title, plus the 1992 and 1993 runs to the championship by the Fab Five were vacated. Webber's All-American honors in 1993 were also forfeited.MORE: Most points in a single March Madness game
